summary: An arrow function such as (s) => s + 5 is a small unnamed function. JavaScript arrays filter and transform with filter(), map(), and reduce(), and each call returns a new array right away.
notes: scores.filter((s) => s >= 70).map((s) => s + 5) chains two steps. The original scores array does not change.
scores.values() makes an iterator. Its filter() is lazy, like a Python filter object or a Java stream, so it can be read only once.
reduce((acc, s) => acc + s, 0) starts at 0, so an empty array returns 0 instead of failing.
pitfall: Calling reduce() on an empty array with no starting value throws TypeError: Reduce of empty array with no initial value.
contrast: JavaScript chains array methods like a Java stream, but each step runs right away and returns a real array that you can reuse. Python usually writes the same work as a list comprehension.
